meta.title: DeAltura Coffee — High-altitude Latin American coffee, roasted in Canada
meta.description: Wholesale specialty coffee from Santa Cruz de Mora, Mérida, grown at 1,600 to 2,000 m and roasted in Canada for cafés and shops.

hero.line1: Single origin from Santa Cruz de Mora, Mérida, Venezuela
hero.line2: Castillo, washed, grown at 1,600 to 2,000 m
hero.line3: Wholesale for cafés and shops across Canada

intro.heading: Altitude is flavour
intro.note: Above 1,600 metres the air is cool and the cherries ripen slowly. Slow ripening makes denser beans with more sugar, which is why this coffee tastes of chocolate and molasses.

facts.explain: Above sea level, in the Andes of Mérida
Fruit removed before drying, for a clean cup
Roast day in Canada, shipped within 48 hours

moments.caption: Picked ripe
moments.text: Growers in Santa Cruz de Mora pick each cherry by hand once it turns deep red.

moments.caption: Washed and dried
moments.text: The fruit is washed away and the beans dry slowly in the sun before milling.

moments.caption: Shipped green
moments.text: Green coffee keeps for months, so it travels north unroasted and freshness starts in Canada.

moments.caption: Roasted on Tuesday
moments.text: We roast to order each week, one profile for espresso and one for filter.

moments.caption: Packed and dated
moments.text: Every bag carries its roast date, so your baristas know what they are pouring.

moments.caption: At your counter
moments.text: Delivered across Canada. Order again from your account in a couple of clicks.

items.q: Do you charge tax on coffee?
items.a: Roasted coffee beans are basic groceries in Canada, so they are zero-rated for GST and HST.
Whole bean only, so the coffee stays fresh until it reaches your grinder.
Both. Pick the roast for each line in your order; the beans are the same, the curve is different.
Venezuela is our flagship, alongside high-grown lots from Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama. New lots arrive with each harvest.

origin.title: Santa Cruz de Mora
origin.lead: A coffee town in the Andes of Mérida, Venezuela.
origin.whyText: High in the mountains the nights are cold and the days are mild. Cherries take longer to ripen, beans grow denser, and the cup gains sweetness and structure. That is the whole idea of DeAltura: coffee from up high.
origin.canadaText: We bring the coffee in green and roast it here, close to the cafés that serve it, so every bag reaches you within days of roasting.
origin.allLead: Each lot sits where it grows. Toronto, where the coffee lands, is at 76 m.
